institution_name: Hypothetical Japanese University — Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science (Synthetic Profile, Fictional)

structural_rules.text: Students must construct a regular expression that recognizes strings over {a,b} with an even number of a's and an even number of b's.
Correctness is demonstrated primarily through examples and verification against a provided acceptance table; a full formal proof is not required at this course level.
Prerequisite knowledge is limited to set notation and basic string operations; finite automata are introduced later in the course sequence and are not assumed at the time of the EE exercise.
AI feedback must be calibrated to the prerequisite level: references to DFA transitions or formal language equivalence theorems are considered out-of-scope for this exercise.
Feedback should explicitly distinguish between syntactic errors (malformed regex) and semantic errors (correct syntax, wrong language) because students at this level often conflate the two.
The course emphasises pattern recognition and verification over proof construction at the introductory stage.
Course Learning Outcome 1: Students can apply basic regular expression syntax to describe simple string patterns.
Course Learning Outcome 2: Students can verify a proposed regular expression by testing against a finite set of example strings.
Course Learning Outcome 3: Students can identify whether a given string belongs to a described language using enumeration, not formal proof.

socio_communicative_norms.text: Feedback is typically delivered with explicit step-by-step guidance; students are expected to follow structured walkthroughs rather than derive corrections independently.
Positive framing is prioritised; feedback phrases errors as areas for improvement rather than outright mistakes.
Technical precision is maintained, but formal notation is introduced gradually with plain-language paraphrases alongside each formula.
